title: Radioactive Decay and Half-Life - Dating Rocks and Fossils
learningObjectives: Explain that half-life is the time for one-half of parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms at a constant rate.
Use the decay equation N = N0 × (1/2)^(t/T) to calculate remaining parent material and estimate ages of geologic materials.

explanations.text: Radioactive decay occurs at a constant rate defined by half-life, the time needed for half of the parent atoms to become daughter atoms.

evidence.quote: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is the length of time required for exactly one-half of the parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms.
